Database connection manager.

Variables:

  • path – Path to SQLite database file.

  • _session – Persistent database session.

Initialization

Initialize database connection manager.

Parameters:

  • path – Path to the SQLite database file.

  • echo – If True, SQL statements will be logged to the standard output. If False, no logging is performed.

  • optional – If True, SQL statements will be logged to the standard output. If False, no logging is performed.

session() → collections.abc.Iterator[autostorage.events.Session]#

Yield the persistent database session.

.. note::

This yields the single, long-lived Session created in __init__, not a fresh session per call — rows returned from queries stay attached, so lazy-loaded relationships keep working after the with block exits. As a result, a Database instance is not safe for concurrent use by multiple threads: check_same_thread=False only allows the underlying DBAPI connection to be used from a different thread than it was created on (e.g. a single background worker), it does not make the Session itself thread-safe.

add(row: autostorage.database.Database.add.RowT) → None#

Add row to session.

.. note::

The row is not validated or written to the database until the next flush() or commit(). Integrity/shape errors (unique constraints, the shape event listeners) raise there, which may be far removed from this call.

add_all(rows: autostorage.events.Iterable[autostorage.database.Database.add_all.RowT]) → None#

Add multiple rows to session.

.. note:: Bulk add(). Same staging-only caveat applies.

merge(row: autostorage.database.Database.merge.RowT) → autostorage.database.Database.merge.RowT#

Merge row into current session and commit, returning the merged row.

merge_from(source_db: autostorage.database.Database, *, commit: bool = True) → autostorage.merge.MergeReport#

Merge another database’s contents into this one.

Unlike merge() (a same-session upsert of a single row), this copies every row from a separate source_db into this database, remapping ids/foreign keys and deduplicating content-unique rows.

This is the recommended entry point for merging from library code; it delegates to autostorage.merge.merge_databases.

.. seealso:: :py:obj:autostorage.merge

flush() → None#

Flush pending changes to the database without committing.

.. note::

Unlike commit(), this doesn’t trigger SQLAlchemy’s default expire_on_commit behavior, so an already-loaded object whose row was removed by a DB-level ondelete="CASCADE" during this flush would be read back stale. expire_all() forces those objects to reload (or raise) on next access instead.
